Step 3 of 10

Travel

Either add a trip and file its costs under it, or enter a travel line on its own. A trip sets where, why and how many times it happens, and every line under it multiplies by that; a line on its own carries its own destination. Either way the kind fixes what is counted, the duration unit, and the schedule rows the rate may come from.

Step 9 of 10

Indirect rate

The rate is not yours to set — it comes from your approved indirect cost rate agreement. What this step asks is which of the nine categories it applies to, because that decides the base, and the base decides the total.

Indirect rate

Single rate

26.75% · NICRA 2026-14, approved 03/11/2026

Effective 05/01/2026 through 04/30/2027 · applied to 7 of 9 cost subtotals

$201,670
Indirect base
scoped subtotals
$53,947
Indirect
at 26.75%

The rate, the document that authorizes it, the period it covers, and — the part that gets checked — exactly which cost subtotals it is applied to. Every change here re-bases the indirect calculation immediately, both below and in the cost grid.

Rate structure

Dual rates are not entered on this screen
A dual rate charges on-site and off-site work at two different rates, and a rate that changes part-way through the contract has to be weighted by the months on each side of the change. Neither calculation is built here — a dual-rate budget is worked out with your contracting officer before the LIB is entered.

What this rate is applied to
